items.prompt: A caller supplies price text "1.234". Why should this source NOT be advertised as a general-purpose rounding parser?

options.text: It automatically applies bankers rounding to any number of decimals.
options.why: The code has no such decimal-scale or rounding procedure.

options.text: Extra digits always mean a zero price.
options.why: There is no such valid-price rule.

options.text: Its public input assumes exactly two fractional digits.
options.why: General parsing and a declared rounding policy require a separate contract, not silent truncation or reinterpretation.

options.text: The public task forbids all prices below one dollar.
options.why: Valid positive prices can include cents; precision grammar is the issue.

items.explanation: General parsing and a declared rounding policy require a separate contract, not silent truncation or reinterpretation.
